subject: Optimize plan split and feature allocation for BriteHealth
messages:
From: Emma Luo <emma@britehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: salesops@britehealth.com, mchen@britehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Plan split and feature gating question

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to move faster / commit to a Dedicated-style contract but have two questions before we present to procurement: 1) We run two product environments (core and pilot). Does Redwood allow a single contract with different feature bundles per environment (e.g., full chat + embeddings for core, limited generation + embeddings for pilot) and how would that affect pricing and seats? 2) If we start with a smaller footprint on pilot and then expand, can we upgrade the pilot tier midterm without penalty (proration or credits)?

Attached is a sketch of the feature matrix we discussed. Can you indicate the delta to the baseline list price and any recommended bundle that reduces unit cost while keeping our compliance posture? Procurement will want clear upgrade/downgrade rules.

Thanks —
Emma Luo
Head of Infrastructure, BriteHealth
---
Attachment: feature-matrix.pdf (application/pdf, 48 KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Luo <emma@britehealth.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan split and feature gating question

Emma —

Appreciate the clear brief and the matrix. Short answers first: yes, you can have a single contract with per-environment feature bundles; and yes, upgrades midterm are supported with pro-rata charging and an option to apply committed spend to the upgraded tier. There are a few levers that materially change unit economics, so I want to outline them and propose a simple recommended path.

High level:
- Contract model: We can do a single enterprise agreement that defines two "deployment profiles" (core, pilot) with separate feature toggles and commit levels. The contract maps each profile to a billing SKU.
- Upgrade behavior: Upgrades are immediate; we bill the delta pro-rata for the remainder of the billing period. If you have committed spend, we can apply remaining credits to the upgraded usage, or offer a one-time credit depending on term length.
- Cost levers: batching/quantization profiles, KV cache sharing between environments, and seat vs consumption mix.

I'll loop in Grace (SE) for technical gating notes and Neha for commercial options. Can you confirm target monthly token/embedding volume per environment (ballpark) and whether pilot needs SOC2 evidence in the short term?

Next step: I'll put together a pro-forma with two scenarios (conservative pilot growth vs aggressive expansion) and three bundle options (pace, balanced, full). Expect that in an hour.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: (none)

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan split and feature gating question

Jonas / Neha —

Notes from a technical gating perspective:
- Feature gating: We can gate chat vs completion at the route-level. Pilot can use a capped generation model (lower max_tokens and static temperature) and still call embeddings.
- Shared KV cache: If pilot and core are in the same VPC we can share cache to reduce token cost for repeated prompts, but that adds isolation complexity — recommend separate caches unless you want aggressive cost-sharing.
- Compliance: If pilot will store customer PII, we recommend pilot on Dedicated with strict KMS key separation. If pilot is synthetic/test traffic, Hosted with PID redaction is fine.

I'll annotate the feature-matrix and highlight which items require Dedicated vs Hosted. Sending that as a reviewed PDF in a sec.

Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: reviewed-feature-matrix.pdf (application/pdf, 62 KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Luo <emma@britehealth.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, salesops@britehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan split and feature gating question

Emma —

Attached is the pro-forma (britehealth_proforma_v2.xlsx) with three scenarios and explicit upgrade/downgrade mechanics. Summary below:

Scenario A — Pace (conservative pilot)
- Pilot: Hosted tier, capped generation SKU, 50k tokens/day baseline; Core: Dedicated small pool with embedding-heavy profile.
- Year 1 estimated ARR delta vs list: -18% with 12-month commit; pilot upgrades pro-rata; no penalty for downgrade but 30-day notice required to avoid early termination admin fee.

Scenario B — Balanced (recommended)
- Pilot: Dedicated micro-pool (isolated KV cache) with ability to burst to core during load; Core: Dedicated standard pool.
- Year 1 ARR delta vs list: -26% with 24-month commit and commit smoothing across profiles. Upgrades apply pro-rata; if you expand pilot into core we offer a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of remaining pilot committed spend if migration happens within first 9 months.

Scenario C — Full (aggressive)
- Both environments fully dedicated, consolidated billing.
- Year 1 ARR delta vs list: -33% with 36-month commit, best unit price; midterm upgrades essentially net-neutral since you re-allocate commit.

Key commercial bullets:
- Add-ons (advanced observability, extended log retention) priced per-GB separately and can be toggled per profile.
- Seat vs consumption: we recommend consumption-heavy for pilot, seat-heavy for core product integrations.

If you want, Neha can propose a final term sheet with exact line-item pricing. Grace's annotated matrix is attached for the gating details.

Next steps: 1) confirm volume estimates, 2) confirm compliance requirement for pilot (SOC2 required Y/N), 3) pick preferred scenario for a draft term sheet.

Thanks —
Jonas
---
Attachment: britehealth_proforma_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 95 KB)

From: Emma Luo <emma@britehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: salesops@britehealth.com, mchen@britehealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan split and feature gating question

Jonas / Team —

This is super helpful, thank you. We discussed internally and are leaning to Scenario B (Balanced) assuming the migration credit applies — procurement flagged that as a key concession. A few follow-ups: 1) Can you confirm the concrete values you used for "50k tokens/day" (avg tokens per request) so we can sanity-check cost modeling? 2) For the migration credit, is it automatic on migration or tied to a signed amendment? Procurement prefers credits applied to the next invoice rather than retro refunds. 3) Grace: please confirm whether pilot on Dedicated micro-pool will change our SOC2 scope (we're trying to avoid a full re-audit now).

If you can send a short term sheet with the Balanced numbers and contract language about the migration credit application model, we can move to procurement review next week.

Best,
Emma
